Splitting into an unmasked main loop plus a masked tail loop made the main loop pingpong (s_setprio present) while the tail stayed plain.

claim: The plain AMD pipeliner can decline a loop silently (no warning; e.g. gfx942 bf16 GEMM without divisibility-16 pointer info stayed unpipelined at num_stages 2-4). claim: llvm_fn_attrs is an experimental HIPOptions field (string or tuple of (name, value) pairs), so it applies to plain @triton.jit and @gluon.jit kernels. make_llir applies it after the backend's own attributes, removing then re-adding each name (user value wins), before LLVM optimization; there is no allow-list, so unknown names are kept in .llir and ignored. Backend attrs it can override: amdgpu-cluster-dims, amdgpu-flat-work-group-size, uniform-work-group-size, amdgpu-waves-per-eu, amdgpu-sched-strategy (gfx1250), denormal-fp-math-f32.

check: python3 $KT/mfma_efficiency.py cap/att/ui_output_agent_1_dispatch_3/se0_*wv*.json cap/att/ui_output_agent_1_dispatch_3/code.json --arch gfx950

claim: mfma_scaled_check.py (no options) sweeps gl.amd.cdna4.mfma_scaled on one tile: operand k_width 4..64 x scales {None, E8M0 via get_mfma_scale_layout} x formats {e4m3, e2m1} x instr_shape {16x16x128, 32x32x64}, printing max relative error vs fp32 (COMPILE_ERR if it does not compile) and the emitted v_mfma ops. A wrong k_width can compile and return wrong numbers. Needs a gfx950 GPU and Triton >= 3.8 with Gluon; device via HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES.
signal: choosing k_width / scale layout for mfma_scaled
check: HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 python3 $SKILL/scripts/mfma_scaled_check.py

claim: parse_correctness.py turns a bench --check stdout or a harness_lib unit-test run into correctness.json. --parse rel|maxdiff (worst value <= --tol), dqdkdv (every dQ/dK/dV <= tol; 'FAILED:' fails), harness (--exit-code is the verdict; per-case JSON with correct=false fails even at rc 0; --tol only tightens). Exit 0 pass, 1 fail, 2 unknown/environment, 3 harness_incomplete.
signal: need a machine verdict from a correctness log
check: python3 $KT/parse_correctness.py --log ut.out --parse harness --exit-code 0 --out correctness.json

claim: parse_pmc.py reads rocprofv3 counter_collection CSVs (pmc_<group>/ layout, older derived/counters layouts, rocprof-compute pmc_perf.csv), filters to one kernel (substring, or --regex; required), averages each counter over dispatches and derives per-unit busy metrics (VALUBusy, MfmaUtil, L2 hit, DRAM bytes, LDS bank conflicts) plus VGPR/AGPR/SGPR/LDS/grid meta. --print-groups lists PMC_GROUPS, one group per rocprofv3 pass; --top-kernel <trace_dir> names the dominant kernel. VALUUtilization is lane activity, not throughput. Stdlib, no GPU.
signal: turn a counter collection into busy / L2 hit / DRAM bytes / bank-conflict numbers
check: python3 $KT/parse_pmc.py prof my_kernel --arch gfx950

claim: patch_async_reinject.py apply|revert|status splices add_coalesce_async_copy into the installed gluon_to_ttgir, armed only by TRITON_GLUON_ASYNC=1 (unarmed is byte-identical to stock). It targets non-native async-copy patterns (8 B/32 B per lane, or a native width split across layout repetitions); native-width async copy lowers without it. Edits site-packages.
signal: async copy with a non-native per-lane width fails to lower

Needs write access to site-packages; affects every process using that install.
signal: need the spliced pass list on disk / an IR diff with splice on vs off
check: python3 $SKILL/scripts/patch_reinject.py status

Written against the 3.6.0 Gluon surface (gl.thread_barrier vs 3.7 gl.barrier; warp_pipeline_stage reported unavailable on 3.6.0).

check: python3 $SKILL/scripts/pipeline_examples_cdna3.py --compile-only --arch gfx942

claim: pipeline_examples_cdna4.py runs authored-overlap Gluon examples for gfx950 (sync staging control, async multi-buffer rings at native direct-to-LDS widths 4 B/16 B per lane, warp_pipeline_stage) with a numerics check (distinct tile per iteration) and an asm op census (ds_write == 0 plus a direct-to-LDS load = real async). --compile-only (automatic without a torch device) AOT-compiles for --arch (default gfx950) and skips numerics. signal: before authoring an async ring / warp pipeline: a compile-checked pattern on this build

(or TILE_PIPELINE_SURVEY_ROOTS) inventories plain-Triton kernels by the pipeline form their source can exercise: A software pipeline (tl.range with num_stages >= 2), B block ping-pong (add_block_pingpong constraints), C async copy / direct-to-LDS; warp_pipeline_stage has no plain spelling. claim: probe_levers.py probes on the current Triton build (no GPU, no kernel launch) whether version/arch-sensitive levers are reachable: num_stages, schedule_hint, loop_unroll_factor, llvm_fn_attrs sched-strategy / agpr-alloc, warp_pipeline_stage, scaled MFMA, pipeliner re-injection. --brief: one line per lever/knob; yes = reachable (default-off), no, unknown (undecided, not no); knob 'dead-declaration' = accepted and ignored by this build, 'live', 'absent'. Needs import triton.
signal: before sweeping a knob, or when a knob sweep gives a flat result
check: python3 $SKILL/scripts/probe_levers.py --all --arch gfx950 --brief

claim: probe.py measure parses compiled artifacts (.amdgcn/.s + Triton metadata json) in a dir and reports ArchVGPR/AGPR, spills, LDS bytes/WG and both occupancy limiters (registers, LDS) in WG/CU, naming the binding one. No GPU. The target comes from the dump's .amdgcn_target; --arch only for unnamed dumps. Without a known target the register term, and without a known LDS/CU (--lds-per-cu) the LDS term, is printed WITHHELD.
signal: registers, spills, LDS/WG or occupancy limiter of a compiled kernel
check: python3 $SKILL/scripts/probe.py measure --dir <ir>/<variant>_c0 --arch gfx950 --json probe.json

claim: probe.py plan sums the resident tensors of a tile plan (--acc name=MxN fp32 by default, --operand name=MxN, --warps) into VGPRs/lane and the reachable waves/SIMD; a lower bound on what the compiler allocates, not a measurement. No GPU. --arch is required (standalone/kernel_tools copy); the pack's legacy skill-dir probe.py defaults plan to gfx950 with a stderr notice.
signal: does a tile / num_warps change still fit the register file before compiling
check: python3 $SKILL/scripts/probe.py plan --arch gfx950 --warps 4 --acc acc=128x128 --operand a=128x64

claim: profiler_deps.py inspects, in the environment it runs in, rocprofv3/rocprof-compute CLIs, ATT decoder candidates and PMC/trace support, without GPU work or installs, and prints a JSON report; exit 0 means the report was produced (read statuses). llvm_dual_load.llvm_dual_load.status = duplicate_inode means two libamd_comgr.so.3 copies are on disk; on some rocprofv3 releases this aborts every mode once torch/Triton is loaded ('Option ... registered more than once'), on others (rocprofv3 1.3.5 in a Triton 3.8.0 image) trace/pmc/att still run, so the status is a risk flag; one rocprofv3_safe.sh --kernel-trace run confirms (rc 7 = abort). Decoder states: external_candidate, sdk_managed_unverified, decoder_absent, decoder_incompatible, unsupported_cli.
signal: profiler aborts or ATT is missing: is the image's profiler stack usable
check: python3 $KT/profiler_deps.py --att-only
keys: LLVM ERROR: inconsistency in registered CommandLine options

claim: recover_gluon.py is the older text-level recovery driver: from a plain .ttgir it emits a layout factory (default), with --with-skeleton runs triton_to_gluon_translator on --kernel module.path:object (peels @triton.autotune/@triton.heuristics), --with-pipeline appends the async double-buffer scaffold, --verify diffs --anchor-ttgir layouts as a text set (sound one way only), --record emits the transcribe record, --harness runs a command looking for CORRECTNESS PASS. Does not recover register allocation. No GPU; translator needs Triton 3.8 spelling (3.6/3.7: translater).
signal: need an assembled Gluon anchor / translator skeleton from a plain kernel
check: python3 $SKILL/scripts/recover_gluon.py --ttgir ir/plain/plain.ttgir --arch gfx950 --with-skeleton --kernel mypkg.kern:my_kernel --out anchor.py

claim: Skill tools print WITHHELD, NOT CALIBRATED or SCOPED TOOL-GAP (or refuse) when data is missing instead of guessing; amd_isa.py exits 3 for queries it cannot answer (e.g. sparse operands, runtime-selected F8F6F4 widths), and records tagged _conf:uncertain have self-contradicting sources. These tokens mark evidence gaps, not answers.
signal: those tokens in tool output; rc 3

claim: rocprofv3_safe.sh runs one rocprofv3 collection (--pmc "A B" | --kernel-trace | --att | --att-wide) with a kernel regex filter, a timeout (default 150 s; --no-timeout) and artifact checks, writing <out>/rocprofv3_safe.json (state collected|partial|unavailable|failed, reason, rc) and rocprofv3.log. Exit 0 ok, 124 timeout, 2 usage/lock, 3 dependency/locus, 4 no matching artifacts, 5 partial, 7 llvm_dual_load, 134 abort (split the PMC group). --att code null = no wave on the traced CU (KT_ATT_TARGET_CU). Needs rocprofv3 + GPU; --gpu takes gpu_lock.sh. capture.sh uses PROFILE_PMC_TIMEOUT 150 / PROFILE_ATT_TIMEOUT 600; a caller timeout shorter than these orphans the profiler.
signal: need hardware counters / kernel trace / ATT for one kernel with a guarded profiler call
check: bash $KT/rocprofv3_safe.sh --kernel 'my_kernel' --out prof --pmc "SQ_WAVES SQ_BUSY_CYCLES" --gpu 0 --cmd "python3 bench.py"

check: W=$PWD/work; mkdir -p $W; bash $SKILL/scripts/runtime_env.sh prepare --work $W --container-work /work --run-id r1 --out $W/runtime-env.json

claim: smoke_layout_gpu.py --out <new dir> validates gfx950 layouts: suite core (native FP16/BF16/MXFP4 GEMMs + trivial-swizzle copy-back controls) or staging (candidate swizzle/padding copy-back; not a supported-layout list); per-case artifacts and status. Exit 0 all pass, 1 failure, 3 incomplete/unsupported without failures. --compile-only: no GPU/lock, AOT-compile + expected MFMA opcode check, status 'compiled', numerics not checked. No timing.

claim: ttgir_bridge.py recover --ttgir <plain.ttgir> --arch <gfx> parses the TTGIR with the compiler's parser and converts each layout via upstream layoutToGluon into Gluon layout constants (--out) + JSON facts (--json), with per-use-site provenance, a round-trip proof per layout, compiled buffer_load forms and an LDS allocation sum (elements, no liveness). Exit 1 when any layout is UNRECOVERABLE (unless --allow-unrecoverable); exit 4 when the num_warps cross-check FAILs. --arch required. Needs import triton (>=3.7 full); no GPU.

check: python3 $SKILL/scripts/ttgir_bridge.py recover --ttgir ir/plain/plain.ttgir --arch gfx950 --out layouts.py --json facts.json
